title: Linux Disk Management Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on checking disk space, identifying block devices, partitions and filesystems, mounting, persistent mounts via /etc/fstab, swap, and tracking down what fills a disk.

chapters.title: Disk Stack Mental Model and Checking Space
points: Layers bottom to top: block device (/dev/sda, /dev/nvme0n1) -> partition (sda1, nvme0n1p1) -> filesystem (ext4, xfs) -> mount point (a directory); a disk is unusable until it has a filesystem and is mounted
df reports free space per mounted filesystem (reads filesystem metadata); du reports space used by files under a path (walks the directory tree)
df -h gives human-readable sizes, df -hT adds the filesystem type, df -i shows inode usage; a disk can be 'full' with free blocks if inodes run out (many tiny files)
du -sh /var/log = one total for a directory; du -h --max-depth=1 /var = one line per subfolder; add | sort -h to rank them
df and du disagree when a deleted file is still held open by a running process: space stays used until the process closes it or restarts (check with lsof +L1)

chapters.title: Identifying Disks, Partitions and Filesystems
points: lsblk lists block devices as a tree (disk -> partitions -> mount points); lsblk -f adds FSTYPE, LABEL, UUID and MOUNTPOINT columns
blkid prints the UUID, LABEL and TYPE of each device; needs root to read devices it cannot probe from cache: sudo blkid
Partition table types: MBR (max 2 TB disks, 4 primary partitions) vs GPT (disks over 2 TB, 128+ partitions); fdisk handles both, parted/gdisk are common alternatives
Create a partition with sudo fdisk /dev/sdb (n new, w write); partitioning does not make a filesystem, you still need mkfs
Format with mkfs: sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1 or sudo mkfs.xfs /dev/sdb1; ext4 can shrink and grow, xfs can only grow; mkfs destroys existing data, so confirm the device name with lsblk first

chapters.title: Mounting and Unmounting
points: mount attaches a filesystem to a directory: sudo mkdir /mnt/data && sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/data; the directory must exist, and any files already in it are hidden while mounted
mount with no arguments or findmnt lists current mounts; findmnt shows a clean tree with source, target, type and options
umount takes the mount point or the device: sudo umount /mnt/data; it fails with 'target is busy' if a process is using it or your shell is cd'd inside
Find what blocks an unmount with lsof +f -- /mnt/data or fuser -vm /mnt/data; umount -l (lazy) detaches now and cleans up later, a last resort
Manual mounts vanish on reboot; use mount -o ro,noexec for read-only or restricted mounts, and mount -a to apply everything in /etc/fstab

chapters.title: /etc/fstab and UUIDs
points: /etc/fstab lists filesystems to mount at boot, one per line with 6 fields: device, mount point, type, options, dump, fsck pass
Example line: UUID=3f2a-... /mnt/data ext4 defaults,nofail 0 2; dump is almost always 0; fsck pass is 1 for root, 2 for others, 0 to skip
Use UUID= (from blkid or lsblk -f) instead of /dev/sdb1: device names like sdb/sdc can change between boots or when disks are added, UUIDs stay with the filesystem
nofail lets boot continue if the disk is missing; without it a bad or absent entry can drop the system into emergency mode
Always test before rebooting: sudo mount -a (errors show up immediately) and findmnt --verify; keep a backup of fstab before editing

chapters.title: Swap and Finding What Fills a Disk
points: Swap is disk space used as overflow when RAM is full; check with swapon --show and free -h
Swap file setup: sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile; chmod 600 /swapfile; mkswap /swapfile; swapon /swapfile; permanent with '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' in fstab
Swap partition: mkswap /dev/sdb2 then swapon /dev/sdb2, referenced in fstab by UUID with type swap; turn off with swapoff
Disk full workflow: df -h to find the full filesystem, then du -h --max-depth=1 / 2>/dev/null | sort -h to drill into the biggest folder, repeating one level deeper each time
Usual culprits: /var/log (rotate or vacuum with journalctl --vacuum-size=200M), Docker data in /var/lib/docker, old package caches, core dumps; find big files with find / -xdev -type f -size +500M

chapters.title: Disk Commands Cheat Sheet
points: Space: df -hT (usage and type), df -i (inodes), du -sh <path>, du -h --max-depth=1 . | sort -h
Devices: lsblk -f, sudo blkid, sudo fdisk -l
Prepare: sudo fdisk /dev/sdX, then sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdX1
Mount: sudo mount /dev/sdX1 /mnt/x, sudo umount /mnt/x, findmnt, fuser -vm /mnt/x
Persist: UUID=<uuid> /mnt/x ext4 defaults,nofail 0 2, test with sudo mount -a
Swap: mkswap, swapon, swapoff, swapon --show; fstab line '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0'
Disk full: df -h, then du drill-down, find / -xdev -size +500M, lsof +L1 for deleted-but-open files
